title: Webb County commissioners press pause on two big price tags: courthouse work and a parking lot
excerpt: Webb County commissioners questioned a $685,000 courthouse architectural contract and a $300,000 parking-lot figure at their Oct. 27 meeting, KGNS reported.
content:
Webb County commissioners questioned a $685,000 architectural contract and a $300,000 parking-lot figure at their Oct. 27 meeting, KGNS reported, putting two county spending items under public scrutiny in a single session.

The courthouse item centers on an agreement with Steven Land Tillotson Architect, PLLC, for the Webb County Courthouse Rehabilitation Project, according to KGNS. Commissioners debated whether all of the proposed work is actually needed to meet a January grant application deadline.

The building at issue is 115 years old and needs extensive repairs to windows, doors, floors and heating, ventilation and air-conditioning systems, KGNS reported. That age and scope are the backdrop for the commissioners' questions: what work is essential, what work can wait, and what happens to the grant timeline if the scope changes.

The parking lot question

Separately, commissioners questioned what they described as a steep $300,000 cost tied to a 20-space lot for the Community Action Agency Administration (CAA) Building, KGNS reported. Officials acknowledged the CAA building needs more parking, but pressed contractors on the expense.

At $300,000 for 20 spaces, the figure works out to $15,000 per space. That arithmetic does not by itself settle whether the figure is reasonable: the public summaries reviewed did not break out design, construction, drainage, lighting, accessibility work or other line items, and commissioners' core complaint was about the total, not a single line.

One commissioner framed the exchange as a duty to taxpayers, saying, in part, “It’s our fiduciary job to be able to say, ‘Wait a minute here.”

What remains unclear

The KGNS summaries reviewed did not state the final disposition of either item — whether it was approved, amended or deferred — and a Spanish-language report of the same meeting described the courthouse contract as approved. The meeting record, not either summary, settles that question, along with the itemized scope behind each figure and the exact January grant deadline at stake.

Those are the documents residents should be able to see: the contract scope for the courthouse work, the cost breakdown for the CAA lot, and the grant application the January deadline serves. Until those are public in full, the $685,000 and $300,000 figures are questions, not verdicts.
